rich_summary: As the climactic battle between Rama and Ravana resumes, Ravana orders his charioteer to drive him straight back into combat, refusing to retreat until his enemy is destroyed. Meanwhile Rama stands momentarily exhausted on the battlefield. At this critical moment the sage Agastya appears among the assembled gods and reveals a sacred teaching: the Aditya Hridaya, a hymn to the Sun. Agastya explains that the Sun is the cosmic source of creation, time, energy, and victory, honored by gods and demons alike. Reciting this eternal hymn dispels fear, grants strength, and ensures triumph in peril. Rama meditates on the Sun, chants the hymn, purifies himself, and regains courage and clarity, preparing to confront Ravana again. The episode frames the coming victory as both martial and cosmic, aligning Rama with divine order and solar power.

Rama's grief lifts as he meditates on the Sun and regains strength before resuming the battle.

top_scenes.scene_text: The sage Agastya appears radiant among gathered gods on the battlefield and instructs the weary Rama while Ravana waits in his towering war chariot.
Rama stands in the war-torn field at dawn, hands folded toward the blazing Sun as he recites the Aditya Hridaya while armies pause around him.
Ravana's massive chariot thunders forward across the battlefield, the demon king crowned and furious as he charges toward Rama.
